To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed SSC tracking loop achieves the superior noise resiliency and timing accuracy and can significantly improve the timing performance of digitally controlled CDR loops.

a novel SSC tracking aid for digitally-controlled clock and data recovery loops is presented, which achieves the superior noise robustness and SSC timing accuracy by employing an integration based mean tracking algorithm.

the proposed SSC tracking loop achieves superior noise resilience and accuracy in recovering the deflection timings of the incoming SSC profile, which in turn improves the timing margin of digitally controlled CDR loops by 1.57 times in case of tracking 6 Gb s data stream modulated by a 30 kHz triangular SSC profile.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of the proposed SSC tracking loop for digitally controlled CDRs.
developing a new tracking aid for SSC modulated signals, which is accurate in recovering the SSC timing instants and resilient to noise.
the design of a new spread spectrum clock (ssc) tracking aid for a digital clock and data recovery loop.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed tracking aid is accurate, robust, and simple, and therefore it is a promising alternative to the existing SSC tracking aid solutions for high speed data communication applications.
the proposed tracking aid is accurate and robust to the SSC profile noise and hence is well suited for high speed serial data communication links employing SSC clocking.
the presented tracking aid is an accurate and noise resilient solution that can be employed for improving the performance of digitally controlled CDRs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed SSC tracking aids can be employed to improve the timing margin of a digitally controlled PLL or DLL based CDR, when recovering the SSC deflections.
the proposed SSC tracking aids can be employed to achieve a significant reduction in the jitter of digitally controlled PLL based CDRs.
a 1.5 % SSC timing error can be tolerated in a 10 Gb/s data recovery application, which corresponds to 0.75 UI timing error.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed SSC tracking loop is a viable solution for improving the timing performance of digitally controlled CDRs.
a tracking aid that can accurately recover the SSC deflection time instants is an effective means for improving the timing margin in CDR circuits.
a simple integration based mean tracking aid can achieve superior SSC tracking performance, which can be exploited to improve the timing performance of digitally controlled CDR loops.
